courses.title: Mini Chubby Honeybee Amigurumi
courses.summary: Craft an irresistible chubby bumblebee with fluttery white wings and safety eyes. Perfect for your very first 3D crochet project!
materials: Plush Chenille or DK Cotton Yarn (Honey Yellow & Licorice Black)

steps.title: Starting the Body (Yellow Yarn)
steps.stitchFormula: Round 1: 6 SC in MR [6] | Round 2: INC in each st around [12]
steps.instruction: Begin with a magic ring using yellow yarn. Work 6 single crochets into the loop, then pull the tail gently to seal the hole. On Round 2, make 2 single crochets into every stitch to expand to 12 stitches.
steps.proTip: Use a stitch marker in the last stitch of each round so you never lose your place when crocheting in spirals.

steps.title: Expanding the Sphere & Color Alternation
steps.stitchFormula: R3: (1 SC, INC) x6 [18] | R4: (2 SC, INC) x6 [24] | R5: SC around in Yellow [24]
steps.instruction: Expand the diameter gradually until you reach 24 stitches. On Round 6, switch to black yarn on the last yarn-over of stitch 24 for a clean color transition without steps.
steps.proTip: Carry unused yarn gently inside the body without pulling too tightly to prevent puckering.

steps.title: Black Stripes & Inserting Safety Eyes
steps.stitchFormula: R6-R7: Black SC around [24] | R8-R9: Yellow SC around [24] | R10: Black SC around [24]
steps.instruction: Work alternating two-round stripes. Before beginning the closing decreases, insert 8mm safety eyes between rounds 7 and 8, spaced approximately 5 stitches apart. Secure firmly with backing washers.
steps.proTip: Embroider a sweet smile with black embroidery floss before stuffing the body firmly with fiberfill.

steps.title: Closing Decreases & Stuffing
steps.instruction: Firmly stuff the body with fiberfill stuffing, shaping it into an oval. Work invisible decreases around. Cut yarn leaving an 8-inch tail, weave through the front loops of the final 6 stitches and cinch closed.
steps.proTip: Use the 'invisible decrease' method (hooking under front loops only) so no holes or stuffing poke out.

steps.title: Crafting & Attaching the Wings
steps.stitchFormula: Make 2: In White, MR: CH 2, 2 DC, 2 HDC, 2 SC, CH 2, SL ST into ring. Pull tight.
steps.instruction: Create two delicate teardrop wings in pure white. Sew securely onto the upper back between rounds 6 and 9 with whip stitches.
steps.proTip: Weave tails deeply inside the plushie so your bee is child-safe and durable.

courses.title: Boho Sunflower Granny Square Tote
courses.summary: Create vibrant dimensional sunflower motifs with puff stitches and cluster petals, joined into an ultra-trendy bohemian shoulder tote.
materials: Aran/Worsted Weight Cotton Yarn (Dark Brown, Mustard Yellow, Cream/Oatmeal, Olive Green)
Woven bag handles (optional) or crochet strap yarn

abbreviations.meaning: Puff Stitch (Yarn over, pull loop x 4, pull through all)

steps.title: Center Seed Puff (Brown Yarn)
steps.stitchFormula: R1: MR, CH 1, 8 Puff stitches with CH 1 space between each. [8 puffs]
steps.instruction: Work into the magic ring to form a rich textured seed center with 8 fluffy puff stitches.
steps.proTip: Keep yarn loops pulled to a uniform 1/2 inch height before finishing each puff stitch.

steps.title: Vibrant Yellow Petals (Mustard Yellow)
steps.stitchFormula: R2: In each CH 1 space, work 4-DC cluster petals separated by CH 2. [16 petals]
steps.instruction: Attach vibrant mustard yarn into any chain space. Work 2 cluster petals into each space to double petal count to 16.
steps.proTip: Pull cluster loops firmly at the crown for pointed, organic sunflower petals.

steps.title: Squaring the Circle (Cream/Oatmeal Yarn)
steps.stitchFormula: R3: Corners: (3 TR, CH 2, 3 TR) | Sides: 3 DC, 3 HDC, 3 DC in successive spaces.
steps.instruction: Transform the round flower into a crisp square motif by distributing treble crochet corners and shorter half-double stitches along the sides.
steps.proTip: Double check you have exactly four 90-degree corners spaced evenly.

steps.title: Blocking & Invisible Seaming
steps.stitchFormula: Make 13 squares total. Steam block each square to 5x5 inches. Join using Mattress stitch.
steps.instruction: Pin out squares on a blocking board and lightly steam to relax fibers. Arrange in 3x3 layout with gusset and join seamlessly.
steps.proTip: Blocking elevates handmade crochet to boutique-grade luxury.

courses.title: Cozy Ribbed Hexagon Cardigan
courses.summary: Construct an effortlessly stylish, oversized drape cardigan using two folded crochet hexagons with plush ribbed cuffs and neckline.
materials: DK or Worsted Acrylic/Wool blend (approx. 700g - 900g based on size XS-3XL)

abbreviations.meaning: (3 DC, CH 2, 3 DC) in same space

steps.title: Laying the First Hexagon Foundation
steps.stitchFormula: R1: MR, CH 3, (2 DC, CH 2) x5, 2 DC, CH 1, SL ST. [6 distinct corners]
steps.instruction: Form a flat 6-sided hexagon. As rounds grow, the shape will naturally ruffle, ready to fold in half into an L-shaped sleeve and torso.
steps.proTip: Count 3-DC clusters on each side every 3 rounds to guarantee symmetrical garment panels.

steps.title: Sizing Up & Folding into Sleeves
steps.stitchFormula: Continue rounds until the side measurement matches your upper sleeve circumference.
steps.instruction: Fold each hexagon in half to form an 'L'. Mirror for right and left halves of the cardigan.
steps.proTip: Try on the sleeves over your clothes before seaming the back and shoulder seams.

steps.title: Seaming Back & Adding Length
steps.stitchFormula: Join back with Slip Stitch seam or Mattress stitch; work bottom hem in back-and-forth rows.
steps.instruction: Join the two halves along the spine. Add extra rows across the lower hem to reach your desired length.
steps.proTip: Use stitch markers to hold the pieces aligned while seaming.

steps.title: Elasticized Ribbed Cuffs & Collar Band
steps.stitchFormula: Switch to 4.0mm hook: Alternate FPDC and BPDC around neckline and wrists.
steps.instruction: Create a tailored elastic cuff and shawl collar using post stitches.
steps.proTip: Post stitches draw in the fabric naturally without any elastic thread needed.

courses.title: Mastering the Magic Ring & Perfect Tension
courses.summary: Never struggle with the adjustable loop again. Master the no-slip 2-finger loop and ergonomic yarn holding for uniform stitches.
materials: Light-colored worsted weight acrylic or cotton yarn (easy to see stitches)

steps.title: The 2-Finger Crossed Loop Technique
steps.stitchFormula: Wrap yarn across index and middle finger forming an 'X' on top.
steps.instruction: Hold yarn tail with thumb. Wrap working yarn over fingers and form an X. Slide hook under first strand and grab back strand.
steps.proTip: Do not pull tight yet; maintain a relaxed circle.

steps.title: Securing with Chain 1
steps.stitchFormula: Yarn over and pull through loop to anchor the ring.
steps.instruction: This initial chain does not count as a stitch, but secures your magic ring so it will not unravel.
steps.proTip: Make sure you crochet over BOTH the loop and the yarn tail together.

steps.title: Working 6 Single Crochets into the Loop
steps.stitchFormula: Insert hook in ring, yarn over, pull up loop (2 loops on hook), yarn over, pull through both.
steps.instruction: Repeat 6 times. Count the 'V' shapes along the top rim to confirm exactly 6 stitches.
steps.proTip: Count stitches before pulling the tail tight.

steps.title: Cinching Tight with Zero Center Gap
steps.stitchFormula: Pull working tail firmly until center hole vanishes entirely.
steps.instruction: Firmly pull the loose tail. The center hole will close seamlessly without puckering.
steps.proTip: Weave in the center tail in opposite directions with a needle so it never opens in the wash.

courses.title: Boho Macramé-Look Crochet Plant Hanger
courses.summary: Craft sturdy hanging baskets for succulents and indoor plants using durable cotton rope and decorative open mesh stitches.
materials: 100% Recycled Cotton Cord or 24-ply twine (150 yards)
Flower pot (4" to 6" diameter for sizing)

steps.title: Solid Bottom Base Disc
steps.stitchFormula: R1: 8 HDC in MR | R2: 2 HDC in each [16] | R3: (1 HDC, INC) around [24]
steps.instruction: Crochet a flat circle matching the bottom base diameter of your plant pot.
steps.proTip: HDC provides a firm, sturdy platform that supports potted plant weight.

steps.title: Building the Diamond Mesh Basket Wall
steps.stitchFormula: CH 4, skip 2 sts, SC into next st around to create flexible cradle.
steps.instruction: Work airy diamond mesh rounds upward to hug the tapered slope of the ceramic pot.
steps.proTip: Slip the pot in periodically to test fit tension.

steps.title: Four-Strand Suspension Cords & Wooden Ring Join
steps.stitchFormula: Divide top rim into 4 quadrants. Chain 60 for each arm. Join to wooden ring with sturdy slip stitches.
steps.instruction: Attach the 4 suspension cords evenly spaced to the wooden ceiling ring.
steps.proTip: Hang on a door handle while tying to ensure all four suspension arms are identical length.

mcqQuestions.question: Which of the following techniques creates a tight, gap-free starting ring commonly used in Amigurumi?
options: Slip knot with chain 10 loop
Magic Ring (Adjustable Ring)
Treble Foundation Chain
Standing Double Crochet
mcqQuestions.explanation: A Magic Ring allows you to pull the tail yarn tight so the center hole completely disappears, preventing fiberfill stuffing from poking through.

mcqQuestions.question: What is the difference between US and UK crochet terminology for 'Single Crochet (SC)'?
options: US Single Crochet is equivalent to UK Double Crochet (DC)
US Single Crochet is equivalent to UK Half Treble Crochet (HTC)
Both US and UK use exactly the same definitions
US Single Crochet is equivalent to UK Slip Stitch
mcqQuestions.explanation: In US terms, Single Crochet (SC) corresponds directly to Double Crochet (DC) in UK crochet terminology.

mcqQuestions.question: What is an 'Invisible Decrease' in Amigurumi and why is it preferred over a standard decrease?
options: Skipping every second stitch without working it
Crocheting through the front loops only (FLO) of two consecutive stitches, creating a smooth finish
Using a hook 3 sizes smaller for the decrease
Cutting and re-joining the yarn with a surgeon's knot
mcqQuestions.explanation: An invisible decrease is performed by picking up only the front loops of two stitches before pulling through, creating a flat, nearly undetectable transition.

mcqQuestions.question: If your crochet project begins curling excessively and cupping upwards when trying to make a flat circle, what is the most likely cause?
options: You are adding too many stitches per round (too many increases)
You do not have enough increases per round, or your tension is too tight
Your yarn is too thick for your hook
You are working in turned rows instead of spirals
mcqQuestions.explanation: Cupping/ruffling occurs when there aren't enough stitches to span the expanding circumference. If it curls into a bowl, you need more increases or looser tension.

mcqQuestions.question: Why is making a 'Gauge Swatch' critically essential before crocheting wearables like sweaters or cardigans?
options: To test if the yarn will shrink in cold water
To verify stitch and row count per 4 inches (10 cm) so the garment fits as sized
To use up leftover yarn before starting the main skein
To practice tying fringe tassels
mcqQuestions.explanation: Crochet tension varies per crafter. A gauge swatch confirms your hook and yarn combination matches the designer's measurements for a perfect fit.

mcqQuestions.question: Which hook size is standardly recommended for Medium / Worsted Weight (Category 4) yarn?
options: 0.75 mm steel hook
mcqQuestions.explanation: Medium worsted weight yarn typically pairs with 5.0 mm to 5.5 mm hooks for balanced drape, though amigurumi often uses 3.5mm-4.0mm for tight fabric.

mcqQuestions.question: In standard crochet pattern notation, what does 'INC' stand for?
options: Insert Needle Carefully
Increase: work two stitches into the same stitch
Incomplete chain
Inverse Needle Count
mcqQuestions.explanation: INC indicates an increase, which means placing two single crochets (or specified stitches) into a single stitch from the previous row/round.

mcqQuestions.question: What is 'Blocking' in fiber arts and how does it transform granny squares and garments?
options: Cutting off yarn tails and burning the tips
Dampening or steaming finished pieces and pinning them to measurements to relax stitches and square edges
Doubling the yarn weight using two hooks
Crocheting around a wooden block frame
mcqQuestions.explanation: Blocking aligns stitch definition, squares out motifs, opens lace patterns, and gives garments professional drape.

mcqQuestions.question: When crocheting a classic 3-DC Granny Square, what usually separates the clusters along the corners?
options: A single slip stitch
A chain-2 or chain-3 space to turn the corner neatly
A treble decrease
Nothing, clusters are stacked directly
mcqQuestions.explanation: Corners in classic granny squares feature (3 DC, CH 2 or 3, 3 DC) in the corner space to produce a clean 90-degree angle.

mcqQuestions.question: What is the primary function of a locking stitch marker when crocheting in continuous spirals?
options: To decorate the finished toy
To mark the first or last stitch of each round so you know when a round completes
To weigh down the center of the ring
To measure yarn yardage
mcqQuestions.explanation: Continuous spirals have no slip-stitch seam, so a stitch marker placed in the final or first stitch keeps your round counts accurate.
